text:
Maria G: FYI I'm seeing some requests for tenant `acme-corp` get routed to the fallback model even though the rule should match their header override.
Ajay P: ugh, saw that earlier. Can you paste a raw decision trace for one of the failing requests?
Maria G: here's one (redacted):
```
route_id: tenant-acme
match: headers.x-tenant == "acme-corp"
eval: false
reason: header-casing-mismatch
headers: {"X-Tenant": "acme-corp"}
```

Samir K: looks like the matcher is comparing `x-tenant` lowercase only. We normalize incoming headers to lowercase in the gateway, but the rule engine expects canonical header keys.
Sylvia L: hmm. That should be covered by the header-normalization layer. Which commit rolled that behavior? @route-bot show last deploy for gateway-proxy
route-bot: deploy 2026-03-01T12:34Z -> gateway-proxy v3.7.2 by ci/cd
Ajay P: I suspect the decision log sampler is dropping some of the full traces; we're only storing the compact decision summary in prod. Need to confirm if the trace we saw was reconstructed from a sparse sample.
Maria G: the request had no decision-log id in the compact record, but the proxy trace id was present: `trace: 8f7a2c`. I pulled the full tracing span from X-Ray and attached above.
Samir K: quick repro: curl -H "X-Tenant: acme-corp" https://gateway/api/v1/chat -> falls back. If I send `x-tenant: acme-corp` lowercase it matches. So mismatch in normalization between the gateway and rule-eval component.
Sylvia L: OK we need a mitigation. Options: 1) Make rule engine lower-case header-aware 2) Have gateway canonicalize header keys to the rule engine format 3) Add a console indicator to show header normalization mismatch for samples.
Ajay P: short term, we can add a canary middleware that forces header keys to lowercase before sending to the evaluator. Low risk, quick. I'll open a change with a canary flag.
Maria G: +1. Also we should fix sampling visibility — we couldn't tell from the dashboard whether the decision log we inspected was complete or sampled. That made debugging slow.
Samir K: agreed. Proposal: add a small badge in the Decision Logs UI that says `sampled: yes/no` and the sampling weight, plus a link to the trace id if available. Should be a single-line change to the UI.
Sylvia L: also add the header-key normalization field in the raw decision trace view (before vs after normalization). That will avoid the guesswork.
Ajay P: I'll send two PRs: middleware canary and UI badge. Can we do an infra task to replay sampled requests for a short window so we can compare pre/post?
Maria G: can we also log an event whenever a rule evaluation fails due to "header-casing-mismatch"? We can treat that as a low-rate metric to monitor.
Samir K: yes I'll add a counter `rule.eval.header_normalization_mismatch` and increment on that code path.
Sylvia L: timeline?
Ajay P: middleware PR today, UI PR tomorrow, metric + alert by EOD. I've created an issue: https://redwood-internal/issue/PLAT-2345 (placeholder).
Maria G: thanks — once middleware is canaried I'll run the curl smoke tests and confirm. Would like the Decision Logs UI badge in next deploy so support can triage faster. :pray:
Samir K: noted. For follow-up: we should audit other matchers (query params, cookie names) for similar normalization blind spots.
Maria G: thanks team — saved me several hours.
Sylvia L: nice catch. :eyes:
